content.title: Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (PESI) and simplified PESI (sPESI)
content.summary: Description of clinical scores integrating pulmonary embolism (PE) severity and comorbidity. PESI is the extensively validated index for identifying patients at low risk for 30-day mortality (PESI classes I and II). A simplified version (sPESI) with fewer weighted variables has been developed and validated; both identify low 30-day mortality risk, and sPESI performance has been confirmed in observational cohorts.
key_points: PESI integrates PE severity and comorbidity; principal strength is reliable identification of patients at low risk for 30-day mortality (classes I and II).
A randomized trial used low PESI as inclusion criterion for home treatment of acute PE.

Original PESI includes 11 differently weighted variables; sPESI is simplified and validated and retains prognostic performance for 30-day mortality, though not yet prospectively used to guide therapeutic management of low-risk PE patients.
content.notes: References to validation studies and observational cohorts are cited (reference numbers present in the source).
